meta.title: Privacy Policy — ianua
meta.description: How the ianua demo collects, uses, and protects your data.

demo.title: This is a demo
demo.body: Ianua is in early development. What you are using is a preview, offered free, with no guarantee of availability and no commitment that anything you put in it will survive. Please read the section on real data below before you enter anything.

responsible.title: Who is responsible
responsible.p1: Ianua is operated jointly by Maurice Schilpp and Giorgi Zoidze as private individuals. There is no company yet.
responsible.p2: Contact for anything in this policy, including requests about your data: <mail>{email}</mail>
responsible.p3: Because we are individuals rather than a company, you are dealing with us personally. We think that is worth stating plainly rather than hiding behind a brand.

collect.title: What we collect, and why
collect.intro: When you create a demo account we store:

email.why: To identify your account and send you verification and password links

displayName.why: To show who you are in the interface

password.why: Stored only as an Argon2 hash — we cannot read it

mfaSecret.what: MFA secret, if you enable it
mfaSecret.why: Encrypted, to check your one-time codes

sessions.what: Session records — session id, IP address, browser user agent
sessions.why: To keep you signed in and to spot suspicious access

audit.what: Audit records — what was done, by whom, when
audit.why: Because an identity system that cannot say who did what is not worth demonstrating

collect.p1: We collect nothing else. There is no analytics, no advertising, no tracking across other sites, and no profiling. We do not sell data — there is no mechanism to do so and no intention.
collect.p2: The legal basis is your consent, given by choosing to create a demo account, together with our legitimate interest in keeping the demo secure. You can withdraw consent at any time by asking us to delete your account.

recipients.title: Who else sees it
recipients.intro: Only the services that make the demo run:

hosting.label: Hosting
hosting.rest: our servers and database, located in the EU

email.label: Email delivery
email.rest: to send verification and password-reset messages

monitoring.label: Error monitoring
monitoring.rest: so we find out when something breaks

recipients.p1: Each processes data only to provide that function. We do not share your data with anyone else, and nobody has bought or been given access to it.
recipients.p2: We are based in Ukraine, so data is accessed from outside the EU when we administer the system.

retention.title: How long we keep it
retention.p1: For as long as your demo account exists, or until you ask us to delete it.
retention.p2: We may reset the demo entirely — including deleting all accounts — as development continues. We will try to give notice, but treat nothing in the demo as durable.
retention.p3: Ask us to delete your account and we will do it, normally within a few days. Backups are overwritten within 30 days, so data can persist there briefly after deletion; we would rather tell you that than imply deletion is instant.

rights.title: Your rights
rights.p1: You can ask us to show you what we hold, correct it, delete it, or send it to you in a portable form. You can object to processing or withdraw consent. Email <mail>{email}</mail> and we will answer within a month — realistically much sooner, since there are two of us and this is a demo.
rights.p2: If you think we have handled your data badly, you can complain to the data protection authority where you live.

noRealData.title: Please do not put real data in the demo
noRealData.p1: Do not use the demo for production systems, real customer data, or anything sensitive. Use test accounts and invented data. The demo has not been through a security audit or a penetration test, it may be reset without warning, and it carries no guarantees.
noRealData.p2: We take security seriously — passwords are hashed with Argon2, MFA secrets are encrypted, access is denied by default, and credentials never appear in logs — but seriousness is not the same as assurance, and we are not going to pretend otherwise while the thing is still being built.

children.title: Children
children.body: The demo is not for anyone under 16.

changes.title: Changes
changes.body: We will update this page as ianua develops. When there is a company behind it, this policy will be replaced by a fuller one and you will be told before that happens.

security.title: Found a security problem?
security.body: Email <mail>{email}</mail>. We will not pursue anyone acting in good faith who tests only their own account, does not access anyone else's data, and tells us before telling the world.

what.title: What this is
what.p1: Ianua is an identity and access management system in early development. This is a free preview, operated by Maurice Schilpp and Giorgi Zoidze as private individuals. There is no company behind it yet, and this is not a commercial service.
what.p2: By creating a demo account you agree to what follows. It is short because there is not much to agree to — you are getting something free that is still being built.

expect.title: What you can expect
expect.p1: Nothing, in the strict sense. The demo may be slow, broken, unavailable, or reset without notice. Features will change. Accounts and data may be deleted as development continues.
expect.p2: We will make a reasonable effort to keep it running and to warn you before wiping it, but there is no uptime commitment, no support obligation, and no service level of any kind.

ofYou.title: What we expect of you
ofYou.intro: Use the demo to evaluate Ianua. Please do not:

items.sensitive: put real customer data, production credentials, or anything sensitive into it — see below
items.illegal: use it for anything illegal, or to authenticate access to anything illegal
items.attack: attack it, load-test it, or try to break it beyond your own account, without asking us first
items.abuse: try to get around limits, or use it in a way that spoils it for others

ofYou.outro: If you do any of these we may remove your account, usually after asking you to stop.

production.title: Do not use this for production
production.p1: The demo is not fit for production use. It has not been security-audited or penetration-tested, it is being actively developed, and it may lose your data.
production.p2: If you use it to protect something real and it goes wrong, that is on you. We are two people offering a preview of unfinished software for free, and we cannot carry the risk of your production systems.

research.title: Security research
research.body: Testing is welcome. Stay within your own account or a test tenant, do not touch anyone else's data, do not degrade the service, and email <mail>{email}</mail> before disclosing anything publicly. We will not take action against anyone acting in good faith on those terms.

data.title: Your data
data.p1: Yours. Ask and we will delete it. What we store and why is in the <privacy>Privacy Policy</privacy>.
data.p2: We do not use your data to train machine learning models.

software.title: <brand>Ianua</brand> the software
software.body: These terms cover the hosted demo only. Ianua's source code, where published, is governed by its own licence, and nothing here restricts the rights that licence gives you.

liability.title: Liability
liability.p1: The demo is provided as is, without warranties of any kind, to the fullest extent the law allows.
liability.p2: We are not liable for loss arising from your use of the demo — including lost data, downtime, or anything that happens to a system you connected to it. This is free, unfinished software offered without charge.
liability.p3: If you are a consumer, nothing here removes rights you have under the law where you live, and we do not exclude liability for death or personal injury caused by negligence, or for fraud. Some of the exclusions above may simply not apply to you, and where they do not, they do not.

ending.title: Ending it
ending.body: You can delete your account at any time. We can withdraw the demo, or your access to it, at any time — and we will withdraw the whole thing eventually, when Ianua becomes a real product.

company.body: These terms will be replaced by proper commercial terms, together with a data processing agreement, once there is a company operating Ianua. You will be told before that happens, and you will not be moved onto a paid plan without agreeing to it.

law.title: Law
law.p1: We are based in Ukraine. If you are a consumer in the EU or elsewhere, the mandatory protections of your own country's law apply to you regardless of anything in this document, and you can bring a claim where you live.
law.p2: For anything else, we would rather sort it out by email than in a court, and given what this is, we expect that will always be possible.

hero.title: <highlight>The front door for your apps</highlight> — and it never lets the wrong person in.
hero.description: Ianua checks who is behind every request — person or AI agent — and whether they're allowed, before it ever reaches your app. Every decision is recorded in a log you can prove wasn't edited.

problem.title: Right now, your access is two tools and a bit of <highlight>hope.</highlight>
problem.body: Most teams wire an identity vendor to a proxy and spread the real rules across config files, the vendor, and app code. It holds together — until the proxy fails and quietly lets traffic through, until the bill grows with every user, until someone asks “who accessed this?” and no one can answer.
problem.closing: Access should fail one way: closed. And it should live in one place you trust.

whoRuns.question: Who runs it?
whoRuns.answer: We do. It is a hosted platform — there is nothing for you to install, operate, patch, or wake up for. Enterprise plans can run the whole thing themselves instead; it is the same code either way.

dataLocation.question: Where does my data live?
dataLocation.answer: In a database of your own, not pooled with anyone else's. You choose the country it sits in, and we hold you to it.

whatIfBreaks.question: What happens if something breaks?
whatIfBreaks.answer: Access fails closed. A missing, unclear, or errored decision is always a no. That is in the core of the system, not a setting someone can leave off.

moveFromOkta.question: Can I move over from Okta or Auth0?
moveFromOkta.answer: Yes. We speak the same standards — OIDC, SAML 2.0, OAuth 2.0, SCIM — so applications already integrated with them keep working. Users and groups come across over SCIM. You can run both side by side and move one application at a time.

versusCloudflare.question: How is this different from putting Auth0 behind Cloudflare Access?
versusCloudflare.answer: Those are two products that do not know each other. The gateway cannot see why the identity provider allowed something, and the identity provider never learns what the gateway did. Ianua is one system, so a decision, its reason, and the rule behind it are a single record.

aiAgents.question: What about AI agents?
aiAgents.answer: Agents are identities, not shared keys. An agent borrows permission from a person — always less than the person has, always time-limited, revocable at any moment — and proves what it is running on with hardware attestation. You can require a human approval before a risky action, see what an agent could reach if it were compromised, and shut it down in one move.

auditProof.question: Can I prove to an auditor that the log is complete?
auditProof.answer: Yes. Every record is hash-linked to the one before it. Walking the chain shows nothing was deleted, reordered, or edited — including by us. Most systems can show you a log; this one can show the log is intact.

standards.question: Which login standards does it support?
standards.answer: OIDC, SAML 2.0, OAuth 2.0, SCIM user sync, mTLS client certificates, passkeys, TOTP, and one-time backup codes. LDAP for software too old to speak anything newer.

perUser.question: What does it cost to add a user?
perUser.answer: Nothing. Pricing is not per user. Adding people is the thing you should be doing least reluctantly.

separation.question: How do you keep customers separate?
separation.answer: Every lookup is scoped to one tenant. Beyond that a tenant can have its own schema, its own database, or its own database in its own country.

changeApps.question: Do I have to change my applications?
changeApps.answer: No. The gateway sits in front and hands your app a verified identity in a signed header. Anything a visitor sent that looked like an identity header is stripped first, so your app cannot be fooled by a header it did not earn.
